disease_label_per_paper: Adult Shiga-toxin mediated hemolytic uremic syndrome masked by alcohol use and inflammatory bowel disease
presentation_summary: 46-year-old man with alcohol use disorder and ulcerative colitis presented with acute alcohol intoxication, 1 month of heavy alcohol consumption, poor nutrition, non-bloody diarrhea, coffee-ground emesis, abdominal pain, weight loss, and falls.
Initial labs showed severe electrolyte abnormalities and lactic acidosis but normal platelets, hemoglobin, and creatinine.
On hospital day 3 he developed epistaxis, hematuria, bruising at IV sites, severe thrombocytopenia, anemia, AKI, high LDH, low haptoglobin, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and schistocytes.
DIC was considered less likely because INR was normal and fibrinogen elevated; stool PCR later returned Shiga toxin 1 positive and ADAMTS13 returned normal.

He initially received ceftriaxone prophylaxis, then presumed TTP treatment with plasma exchange, steroids, and rituximab before transition to supportive care, transfusions, and hemodialysis; he remained dialysis dependent.
